decisions.boundary_condition: Do not generalize this preference to unrelated amenities, room attributes, location, dates, or price, which were not consistently supported by the evidence.
decisions.canonical_value: For leisure-oriented hotel stays, softly prefer rooms that include both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
decisions.condition: When choosing hotels for leisure-oriented stays such as family, vacation, or activity trips.
decisions.default_action: Include an in-room coffee maker and refrigerator or mini-fridge as soft default amenity criteria when searching or comparing hotels.
decisions.exception_condition: If a hotel otherwise strongly matches the trip, confirm a missing coffee maker or refrigerator with the user rather than automatically rejecting the hotel.
decisions.name: leisure hotel room coffee-and-fridge default
decisions.preference_value: Prefer a hotel room with both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
decisions.rationale: Repeated evidence across multiple leisure-oriented hotel searches supports a reusable soft preference for the combination of an in-room coffee maker and refrigerator or mini-fridge. It is distinct from the breakfast preference and should not be broadened to unsupported amenities or treated as a hard filter.

decisions.boundary_condition: Treat free breakfast as a soft default unless the user explicitly makes it mandatory; do not infer a particular breakfast quality standard from the mixed evidence.
decisions.canonical_value: When comparing hotels, softly prefer otherwise suitable options that include free breakfast.
decisions.condition: When searching for or comparing hotels for an overnight trip, after satisfying explicit core constraints such as location, room or bed needs, budget, and required hotel class.
decisions.default_action: Rank or surface hotels with free breakfast higher and confirm inclusion when the amenity is unclear.
decisions.exception_condition: Relax or ignore the preference when breakfast is unimportant, no suitable hotel with free breakfast meets higher-priority constraints, or the user knowingly chooses a hotel without it.
decisions.name: Prefer hotels with included breakfast
decisions.preference_value: Prefer a hotel that includes free breakfast.
decisions.rationale: Free breakfast recurs across multiple hotel requests and is useful as a longitudinal ranking preference. The evidence varies in strength and breakfast-quality expectations, so the supported policy is a soft preference for included breakfast rather than a mandatory filter or a specific quality standard.
